August 25, 1941.

Police Sub-Station in Footung raided by armed group

According to information received, at 11.30 p.m.
August 21, a group of some 100 armed men, under the disguise
of vegetable hawkers and led by 5 or 6 guides, visited the
Police Sub-Station at Yang Sze Chao (楊思橋), Footung.
They asked for Chang Fah Liang (張伯良), Acting Chief
and concurrently head of the administrative section of the
Sub-Station. Chang Fah Liang, however, was absent as he
had returned to his home in Chapei. At that moment, two
sergeants of the Sub-Station named Liu Tseng Chun (劉增君)
and Wang Ching Piao (王金標) raised an alarm and were
shot dead by the intruders. The armed men then took away
with them 2 rifles, 1 pistol and some 90 rounds of ammunition.
The Sub-Station of the Armed Police Corps at Yang Sze Chao
which is under the charge of one Zau Lau Fong (趙志芳)
was subsequently raided by the armed group, who took away
7 rifles from the Sub-Station. The Armed Police Corps is
under the command of Liu Teh Zung (劉鉄城).

Close of ferry jetties by the Japanese Soldiers.

On the morning of December 31, 1940, the
Japanese Military authorities in Nantao closed all
the jetties where the ferries ply between, such as
Nantao, Tungchi, Shihwang, Nan Hsiao Men and Chow
Ka Doo to Tzao Chai; Ping Shing Road and The Chung
jetties are open which are in the Japanese Naval
Defence Area.

It is learned that the troops under the
command of Zee Hoong San (徐鴻茂), commander-
in-chief of the Self Defence Corps at Chuensha,
Pootung, strength about 500, who were formerly
guerrillas and during 1939, surrendered to the Japanese
when they were re-organized into Self Defence Corps,
have become lawless, often robbing and kidnapping.
On December 27, 1940, they robbed the village of Er Ho
Dong (二河塘), Pootung and at 8 a.m. on December
29, the Japanese authorities despatched an interpreter
and four Japanese soldiers to the headquarters of the
Corps at Ding Lo Chao (唐墓橋) to investigate
the incident, but the soldiers of this defence corps
killed the interpreter and two of the four Japanese
soldiers. Those soldiers immediately vacated that
region for San Tsao (三灶), Nanwei where they
are now in hiding. The Japanese Military in conjunc-
tion with some 500 soldiers belonging Ting Sih San,
launched attack on these renegades on December 31,
1940 in order to clear them out and in consequence
they closed all jetties.

Subject Pootung Southern District Administrative Office - Examination of

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Fih Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

During the past week, thirteen primary school
principals have been arrested in Pootung by the Pootung
Southern District Administrative Office because they
have been using textbooks in their respective schools
which are alleged to be of an anti-Japanese nature.
They were subsequently handed over to the Pootung Office
of the Japanese Gendarmerie and it is learned that three
of the 13 arrested principals have since been sentenced
to three months imprisonment.

The Bureau of Education of the Shanghai City
Government have had printed a limited number of textbooks
for use in the primary schools situated in the Japanese
occupied areas. The number of copies printed are only
sufficient for allocation to those primary schools which
are administered by the Shanghai City Government and the
private primary schools are therefore unable to secure
any copies of such textbooks.

Consequently, the private primary schools
obtained textbooks printed by the Shanghai World Book-
stores, which were authorized for use in primary schools
by the Ministry of Education of the Nanking Government
(New Central Government). The Pootung Southern District
Administrative Office nevertheless took exception to the
use of these textbooks and arrested the 13 primary
school principals for using them.

由 侦探督察 潘连璧（Pan Lien Fih）制作 经由 侦探督察 克劳福德（Crawford）转呈。

在过去的一周里，浦东南区行政公署在浦东逮捕了13名小学校长，原因是他们在各自的学校使用了据称具有反日性质的教科书。随后，他们被移交给浦东日本宪兵队办公室，据悉，13名被捕校长中有3人已被判处三个月监禁。

上海市政府教育局印制了有限数量的教科书，供位于日军占领区的小学使用。印制的数量仅够分配给由上海市政府管理的那些小学，因此私立小学无法获得此类教科书的任何副本。

因此，私立小学获得了由上海世界书局印制的教科书，这些教科书经南京政府（新中央政府）教育部批准在小学使用。然而，浦东南区行政公署对这些教科书的使用提出异议，并因使用这些教科书而逮捕了13名小学校长。

Subject Kidnapping in Pootung.

Made by D. I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan

At about 2 a.m., August 17, 1940, Yang Kyung
Hai (楊金海), aged about 30, a native of
Chinkiang, Kiangsu, was kidnapped from his home
at No. 19, Foo Tung Lee, Tung Chong Road, Pootung,
by three male Chinese, two of whom were armed with
pistols.

Yang, it is learned, has been dealing in
heroin in Pootung since the outbreak of the
Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1937, and has amassed
a large fortune.

Information to hand indicates that the
three kidnappers were led to Yang's home by a
girl of about 13 years of age, under the guise
of being heroin purchaser.

On August 18, the Pootung Police Bureau
arrested one named Chang Zung Fah (張順發),
a loafer, who often visited Yang's address for
narcotics, on suspicion of having connections
with this case. The Police authorities there
are endeavouring to effect Yang's release.

Made by D.I. Fan Lien Pih Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

The Pootung Police Bureau of the Shanghai
City Government about one month ago informed the
managements of all foreign owned godowns in Pootung
through their godown keepers to the effect that
the private watchmen in their employ should be
placed under the control of the Pootung Police
Bureau and renamed police-watchmen.
Up to the present, only one foreign concern,
Messrs. Mackinnon Mackenzie & Company, 27 The Bund,
has taken heed of the instruction and the 12 private
watchmen and one sergeant employed at their wharf
at Pootung Point have been renamed police-watchmen
and are under the direction of the Police Bureau
in Pootung. They wear the uniforms supplied by the
Bureau and receive a monthly pay of $35 each in
addition to a rice allowance of $5, while the
sergeant is paid $60 a month as wages (rice allowance
included). They are now paid direct by the Police
Bureau which receives the wages from the company.
Enquiries at Butterfield and Swire Company,
Ltd., French Bund, ascertained that the verbal
instructions are correct, but they do not intend
taking any notice of the request in the meantime.

Subject Japanese Special Service Agent assassinated in Lotung
Made by. D.I. Fa. Lien lih Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

At about 8 p.m., July 8, 1940, HUANG YIN
DEE (黃雲悌), secret agent in the employ of
the Southern Lotung Section of the Japanese
Special Service Department, was fatally shot by
three male Chinese at the home of his concubine
on Tu Dee Dong La, Yang Ka Zah, Lotung Point.
Huang Yin Dee, aged 44, formerly a banker
in Tsunghing, formed a guerilla unit following
the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in
1937 and was soon promoted to the position of a
Company Commander. In Autumn, 1939, he
surrendered to the Japanese Special Service De-
partment and was subsequently appointed a secret
agent attached to the Southern Lotung Section of
the Japanese Special Service Department. A number
of guerilla members operating in the Tsunghing area
have since been arrested by the Japanese authorities
as a result of information supplied by the deceased
secret agent and it is believed that his death was
brought about by his former associates.

Nantao

The supply of rice in Nantao is monopolized by the Nantao Ming Sung Rice and Paddy Association, 377 Min Kuo Road, Nantao, which was formed in March, 1940. The 150 rice shops in Pootung, which suspended business on June 11, 1940, resumed business on June 14 on the instructions of the Japanese Military Police and the Pootung Administrative Office.

At 4 p.m. June 13, ten representatives of the rice shops were called to the Chen Chuoh Road ( 蔡 家 宅 ) Headquarters of the Japanese Military Police, Pootung, where they were lectured on the importance of maintaining the rice supply and instructed them to resume business. A notification instructing the rice shop owners to resume business was also posted outside the Pootung Administrative Office, in which the Administrative Office states that protection will be accorded bona-fide rice dealers while transporting rice supplies.

Under the auspices of the Pootung
Southern District Administrative Office and the
Pootung Section of the Japanese Military Special
Service Department, an "Exhibition of Chinese
and Japanese Paintings and Calligraphy" was held
in the Ming Sing Theatre between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m.
on March 7, 1940. Some 40 large size photographs
of Japanese factories and schools were on display
but there were no exhibits of painting or
calligraphy. The photographs were generally
inscribed "Japan's contribution towards International
Culture."

About 200 persons attended the function,
comprising for the most part children residing in
the vicinity.

The exhibition concluded on March 8,
1940 on which date a closing ceremony was held at
2 p.m. Some 200 persons including representatives
of the various administrative offices in Pootung
and members of the Japanese Special Service organs
in Pootung attended. At the close the following
slogans were shouted:-

1. Enforce the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen's
Pan-Asianism.

2. Support Mr. Wang Ching Wei and his
peace, anti-communist and national reconstruction
policy.

discount on the charges.

(3) Delegates be sent to Japanese wounded
soldiers' hospitals for the purpose
of comforting the inmates with
foodstuffs etc.

village guilds to deliver lectures
on the following subjects :-

Sino-Japanese rapprochement.

Anti-Communist and National Salvation
Work.

Support of the forthcoming new Central
Government.

Establishment of "New Order" in East Asia.

Up to February 16, no propaganda literature had
appeared and no delegates attended village guilds
to deliver lectures.

Date November 30, 1939.
Subject Pootung Administrative Office - Registration
of rice shops in Pootung
Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by

On November 27, a circular notice was issued
by the Pootung Administrative Office of the "Shanghai
City Government" instructing all rice shops in
Pootung to register the stocks held by them with the
authorities. The notice states briefly as follows :
"The recent increase in the price of rice
is found to be due to the hoarding and
manipulation by traitorous merchants. As rice
is the essential food of the people, it is
deemed a necessity to check such unlawful
practice by the merchants. Notice is hereby
issued that with effect from December 1, 1939,
every rice shop must report to and register
with this office in advance the quantities
of rice to be purchased for checking purposes."
Enquiries show that this step has been
taken by the Pootung Administrative Office with the
intention of facilitating the collection of a tax.
Although the rate of levy is not mentioned in the
notice, it is however, known that a sum of 30 cents
will be collected on each picul of rice. The
Administrative Office will issue receipts against
payment of such tax which will grant them the
transporting of their purchases without interference
from the police.

Pan Lien-pih

日期：1939年11月30日。
主题：浦东行政公署——浦东米店登记
撰写人：巡官潘连璧 转呈人：

11月27日，“上海市政府”浦东行政公署发布通令，指示浦东所有米店向当局登记其持有的库存。通告大意如下：
“近期米价上涨，经查系奸商囤积居奇、操纵市场所致。大米乃民众主食，故认为有必要遏制商人的此类非法行为。特此通告，自1939年12月1日起，各米店须事先向本公署申报并登记拟购大米数量，以便核查。”
经查询，浦东行政公署采取此举意在便于征税。虽然通告中未提及税率，但据悉每担大米将征收30分。行政公署将在缴纳税款后出具收据，凭此收据可运输所购大米而不受警方干涉。

潘连璧
巡官

Subject "Southern Pootung Merchants' Federation" (浦东南区商界联合会) -
Formal inauguration.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Fih Forwarded by. C. Gauson

The Southern Pootung Merchants' Federation was formally
inaugurated at a meeting held between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m., on
January 6, 1939, on the former site of the Y.M.C.A. on Tung
Chong Road, Pootung, under the supervision of Mr. Sih Ching
Tsung (薛锦春), Chief of the 3rd Section of the Bureau of
Social Affairs of the "Shanghai City Government." About 30
persons attended the function, including the following:-

Ho Chi-fah (何继黄): Chairman of the Federation; a
native of Ningpo, formerly a fore-
man in the employ of the Kung Dah
No. 2 Cotton Mill; at present owner
of the San Tai(三泰) Coal Hong,
Tung Chong Road, Pootung.

Tsai Ling (崔靈): Vice-Chairman of the Federation;
medical practitioner by profession.

Tsu Ding (朱鼎): Standing committee member of the
Federation; Chief of the Pootung
Branch of the Great People's
Association(大民会).

An executive committee of eight persons including Ma Tung
Hai (马东海), a loafer in Pootung, and a supervisory committee
of four persons including Wong Kwei-ling (王桂林), interpreter
in the office of the Pootung Branch of the Japanese Gendarmerie,
were established while Mr. Watai (渡井), Chief of the Pootung
Branch of the Japanese Gendarmerie, was invited to serve in
the Federation as Senior Advisor.

While delivering his speech during the inaugural ceremony,
Tsu Ding stated that the Chiang Kai-shek Government has been
attempting to further its own ends by sacrificing the Chinese
people; that Japan has taken up arms to exterminate Communism
for the salvation of the Chinese people and that the real
aggressor nations are Great Britain, France, the United States
of America and the U.S.S.R.

D.C.(Sp. Br.)
Pan Lien-pih
D. I.

主题：“浦东南区商界联合会”——正式成立。

撰写人：巡官潘连璧 转呈人：C. Gauson

浦东南区商界联合会于1939年1月6日下午1时至4时，在浦东同宗路前青年会旧址举行会议，正式宣告成立。会议由“上海市政府”社会局第三科科长薛锦春先生主持。约有30人出席了该活动，其中包括以下人员：

何继黄：联合会主席；宁波人，原为公大第二棉纱厂领班；现为浦东同宗路三泰煤号老板。

崔靈：联合会副主席；职业为医师。

朱鼎：联合会常务委员；大民会浦东分会会长。

会议成立了由八人组成的执行委员会，其中包括浦东无业游民马东海；以及由四人组成的监察委员会，其中包括日本宪兵队浦东分会翻译王桂林。同时，邀请日本宪兵队浦东分会会长渡井（Watai）先生担任联合会高级顾问。

朱鼎在成立典礼上发表演讲时称，蒋介石政府一直试图牺牲中国人民以谋取私利；日本为了拯救中国人民而拿起武器消灭共产主义；真正的侵略国家是英国、法国、美利坚合众国和苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟。

CHAMBER OF COMMERCE BEING FORMED

The Shanghai Special Municipal Government
is contemplating the formation of a Chamber of Commerce
in each of the districts surrounding Shanghai. They will
be placed under the control of the Political Affairs
Administration of the district. A General Chamber of
Commerce will also be formed to supervise the other chambers.
A Chamber of Commerce was inaugurated
yesterday in Pootung with one Ho Chi-fah (何志發), native
of Ningpo, formerly an interpreter to the Japanese Naval
Landing Party, as Chairman, and one Tsai Ling (蔡靈) as
his deputy. This Chamber will collect a monthly subscription
from the shops in the district.
It is learned that similar chambers will
be formed in the Western District and in Nantao.

商会正在组建中

上海特别市政府正考虑在上海周边各区组建商会。这些商会将由各区政务管理局管辖。还将组建一个总商会来监管其他商会。
昨日，浦东商会正式成立，由宁波人何志發担任主席，他曾任日本海军陆战队翻译；蔡靈任其副手。该商会将向区内商铺收取月费。
据悉，西区及南市也将组建类似的商会。
